items.question: What is my educational background?
items.answer:
I earned a Master of Computer Science from the University of Wollongong in Australia, scheduled from July 2023 to September 2025 [[cite:3]]. Prior to that, I completed a Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science & Engineering with a Data Science specialization at Gujarat State Fertilizers and Chemicals University (GSFC University) in Vadodara, India, graduating in May 2023 [[cite:3,8]].  

My coursework covered a broad range of foundational and advanced topics, including mathematics, programming languages (C++, Java, Python), data structures, algorithms, operating systems, computer networks, web technologies, as well as specialized subjects such as machine learning, big data analytics, computer vision, modern cryptography, and security [[cite:4,7]]. I achieved high distinctions in programming, data structures, web development, strategic network design, and the professional capstone project, and earned distinctions in big data analytics, security essentials, AI and cybersecurity, and system analysis and project management [[cite:5]].

items.answer: I have worked with a range of AI/ML frameworks and libraries, including scikit‑learn, PyTorch, LangChain, LlamaIndex, FastAPI, Sentence‑Transformers, and rank‑bm25, as well as tools for hybrid retrieval, vector databases (e.g., ChromaDB), embeddings, prompt engineering, multi‑agent orchestration, and LLM evaluation harnesses [[cite:1,4]].

items.question: What internships have I done?
items.answer:
You completed an Android Application Development internship at TSPL in Vadodara from January 2023 to July 2023, where you built an end‑to‑end Android app with backend REST APIs and analytics charts using Java/Spring Boot and MySQL [[cite:1]].  
You also worked as an Engineering Intern (Full Stack + Multi‑Domain) at Gurukula, Tntra Engineering in Vadodara from June 2022 to December 2022, building and shipping web‑app modules and receiving multi‑domain training under senior developer guidance [[cite:1]].

items.question: What awards have I received?
items.answer:
I have received the IEEE Best Paper Award at the 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Speech Technology (AIST 2022) for the paper *Cognitive‑Chair: AI based advanced Brain Sensing Wheelchair for Paraplegic/Quadriplegic people* [[cite:1,3]].  

I am an Indian Government patent holder for an “Intelligent Face Recognition System using Deep Recurrent Neural Network” [[cite:1]].  

I was honored with the Achiever’s Award from GSFC University, Vadodara, for my B.Tech. Computer Science and Engineering programme (2021‑22) [[cite:2]].

items.question: What projects have I built?
items.answer:
I have built a RAG service called **PersonaQuery**, which combines LangChain, LlamaIndex and Llama‑3.3‑70B with hybrid dense‑plus‑sparse retrieval, a golden‑set evaluation harness, and a FastAPI backend that is containerised and production‑ready [[cite:2]]. I also created **HealthEcho**, an end‑to‑end anomaly‑detection and inference pipeline built with scikit‑learn, FastAPI, Docker and CI/CD, taking raw data through to a deployed endpoint [[cite:2]].

Another notable project is **JobPilot**, a six‑stage autonomous job‑application pipeline that scrapes multiple job sites with Playwright, normalises listings using Claude APIs, scores matches, generates LaTeX resumes, produces cover letters with an actor‑critic model, and automatically fills and submits application forms, also routing applications based on ATS detection [[cite:8]].

During my internship at TSPL I built an Android application from scratch, designing clean REST APIs, analytics charts and a full UI‑API‑database stack using Java, Spring Boot and MySQL [[cite:5]].

While interning at Gurukula, I developed and shipped several web‑application modules as part of an industry workflow, gaining experience across full‑stack development, cloud services and security under senior guidance [[cite:5]].

items.question: What is the title of the patent?
items.answer: The patent is titled **“Intelligent Face Recognition System Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network.”** [[cite:1,2,4]]

items.question: What is the patent application number?
items.answer: The patent application number is 202211058943 A [[cite:2,3,4,5]].

items.question: What neural network architectures does the patent describe?
items.answer: The patent discloses a face‑recognition system that combines a **convolutional neural network (CNN)** with a **recurrent neural network (RNN)** to generate a consistent key value from facial images [[cite:6]]. This combination is referred to in the title as a “deep recurrent neural network,” indicating that the RNN is employed in a deep architecture alongside the CNN [[cite:3]].

items.question: What is the patent journal number?
items.answer: The patent journal number is 42/2022 [[cite:1,3]].

items.question: What is the Cognitive-Chair project about?
items.answer: The Cognitive‑Chair is an AI‑driven wheelchair that enables paraplegic and quadriplegic users to control the device using brain‑derived signals rather than physical input. [[cite:4]] It captures electro‑oculography (EOG) and electro‑encephalography (EEG) data via a headband, sends the signals to a mobile application, and translates them into commands that drive the wheelchair. [[cite:3]] The system was created as part of a B.Tech project at GSFC University and was recognized with the Best Paper Award at the 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Speech Technology (AIST‑2022). [[cite:4,7]] The research also led to an Indian government patent for a related intelligent face‑recognition system using deep recurrent neural networks. [[cite:5,6]]

items.question: What are the main brainwave frequencies mentioned?
items.answer: The documents identify five primary brainwave frequency bands—Gamma, Beta, Alpha, Theta, and Delta—as the main frequencies measured by electroencephalography [[cite:1,2]]. These five bands are repeatedly described as the core EEG frequency categories in the source material [[cite:1,2]].

items.question: What microcontroller is used in the wheelchair design?
items.answer: The wheelchair design utilizes an Arduino microcontroller to process the data from the Android application and control the wheelchair’s motors [[cite:1]].

items.question: Which bluetooth module does the system use?
items.answer: The system uses the HC‑06 Bluetooth module for wireless transmission of signals [[cite:2]].

items.question: What is a Brain-Computer Interface according to the paper?
items.answer: A Brain‑Computer Interface (also called a Brain‑Machine or Direct Neural Interface) is a technology that enables users to communicate with and control machines or external devices directly through brain signals, bypassing the normal output pathways of peripheral nerves and muscles【cite:1,2】.  A BCI system typically consists of electrodes that record brain activity, a processing pipeline that extracts and decodes relevant features, and a computer or device that executes the resulting commands【cite:5】.
